findings.description: The tuple-wrapping check was changed from `isinstance(filename, str)` to `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)`, so a plain `str` filename is no longer wrapped in a tuple and is passed straight to `ed.edit_files`.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a caller runs `click.edit(filename='notes.txt')`. The str is not PathLike, so it skips the wrap and reaches `edit_files(filenames='notes.txt')`. That method iterates the argument, so it treats each character as a separate file, opening files named 'n', 'o', 't', and so on. The intended single-file edit of 'notes.txt' does not happen, and the editor is pointed at unrelated or nonexistent paths.
